answer: Agents could require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it can earn trust-weighted rewards. A Sybil attacker must split a finite stake across many accounts, leaving each with less influence, or acquire more tokens and pay the opportunity cost while they are locked. This makes a hollow identity costly to multiply; a fable about free accounts cannot evade the ledger, and a whisper campaign still needs funded identities to affect rewards.
